findings.title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import time, not per instance
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` runs once when the module is imported, so every AssignmentSource created in the process gets the same timestamp: the process start time. The field is meant to record when the assignment was queued, but it will be wrong for every instance. Use a default factory (`field(default_factory=timezone.now)`) or set it explicitly at creation.

findings.title: to_dict() returns a datetime that is passed through Celery task kwargs
findings.body: `to_dict()` uses `asdict(self)`, which keeps `queued` as a `datetime` object. The result is passed as `assignment_source_dict` into `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(...)`. If Celery uses the JSON serializer, which is typical for Sentry, a datetime cannot be encoded and enqueueing fails. On the consuming side, `from_dict` also receives `queued` as a string rather than a datetime, so the round-trip does not preserve the field type. Serialize `queued` to an ISO string (or drop it) in `to_dict`, and parse it back in `from_dict`.

findings.title: No test that deassign with a matching assignment source skips outbound sync
findings.body: The new `assignment_source` parameter on `GroupAssignee.objects.deassign` and the matching-source short-circuit are only exercised for `assign`. `test_assignee_sync_outbound_unassign` only checks the `assignment_source=None` path. The inbound unassign path (`sync_group_assignee_inbound` with `assign=False`) is the one that can create the Jira-to-Jira loop, and it is untested for the case where the source integration matches the target. Add a test that deassigns with a matching `AssignmentSource` and asserts `sync_assignee_outbound` is not called.
